findings.claim: The learning window and score clock are [0.0, 0.5] with 50 observed score nodes at 0.01 spacing; curve support is [0.0, 0.49], so no extrapolation beyond the observed nodes is licensed.
The objective is final predicted target affinity primary, with validity and strain secondary and coordinate control only; coordinate contrasts are therefore proxies, not affinity measurements.

The landmark_00_soft_mass curve over the observed support [0.0, 0.49] rises from about -0.37 z early to a peak near +1.64 z around node 0.16, then declines to about -0.28 z at the last node, with 4 sign changes and only 1 strong sign conflict; the whole-window z is small (about 0.64) and no polynomial is accepted.

Across the 20 landmark soft-mass features, whole-window z magnitudes are small (largest |z| about 0.64 for landmark_00_soft_mass) and no polynomial trend is accepted for any feature, so no landmark soft-mass feature shows a stable whole-window monotone drift.

Endpoint rate contrasts are large and sign-changing: e.g. landmark_00_soft_mass first_rate_z about +9.3 and last_rate_z about -10.0 with 4 sign changes, and landmark_10_soft_mass first_rate_z about +66.3 and last_rate_z about -11.6 with 4 sign changes; these are changing contrasts, not a stationary target.

Strong sign conflicts are present for most landmarks (e.g. 17 for landmark_15_soft_mass, 14 for landmark_09_soft_mass, 11 for landmark_04_soft_mass), and relative node RMSE is high (about 0.29 to 0.99), so per-landmark temporal direction is not reproducible across batches.
Stage profiles and temporal profiles are not available in this delivery; only continuous curves and summary tables are supplied, so no data-derived stage knot is supported.

hypotheses.direction: test staged blend of observed-forecast and static teachers; do not reverse the affinity objective
hypotheses.falsifier: if the staged blend produces no reproducible change in the landmark_00_soft_mass contrast trajectory versus the constant-blend control at fixed dose, the stage-dependent relevance is not supported
hypotheses.observable: landmark_00_soft_mass endpoint contrast curve over score nodes 0.0-0.49
hypotheses.scope: all seeds on the observed score nodes; no extrapolation
hypotheses.statement: A stage-dependent teacher-relevance schedule (early same-clock historical forecasts blending toward frozen static teachers) is worth testing at fixed dose, because the observed landmark_00_soft_mass contrast rises then falls within the window rather than holding a stationary direction.

hypotheses.direction: test regional rather than global delta_A change
hypotheses.falsifier: if no landmark shows a reproducible low-conflict regional shift, delta_A change is not supported
hypotheses.observable: per-landmark soft-mass contrast spread and sign-change count across the window
hypotheses.scope: landmarks with low strong_sign_conflicts and stable sign profile
hypotheses.statement: A geometric response-scale (delta_A) change is worth testing only if the soft-mass contrast spread and covariance show a reproducible regional shift; current whole-window z values are small and sign conflicts are high, so a global delta change is not yet justified.

limitations: No decoded final affinity labels are available; selection and survival are not evidence of final affinity improvement.
Stage profiles and temporal profiles are absent, so no data-derived stage boundary can be claimed.
Coordinate contrasts are untyped proxies; no energy or chemical-interaction interpretation is made.
Whole-window z values are small and polynomial trends are rejected, so no absolute coordinate target or spatial gradient is inferred from the contrast curves.
